title: Directional Rate Ceiling & Session Minimums Probe (hosted API per-token)
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Objective: Validate a hybrid per-token pricing model that applies asymmetric input/output rates with an optional per-session minimum for streaming sessions. Background: Customers and partners have asked for more predictable billing for long-running streams and for clearer cost signals when outputs dominate costs. Hypothesis: Introducing a directional output-weighted ceiling plus a small per-session minimum for streaming can (1) reduce bill surprises for conversational apps, (2) preserve fairness for high-ingest but low-output workloads, and (3) be acceptable to enterprise buyers when surfaced in the SQ and contracts. This ticket captures the experiment design, telemetry needs, and enterprise questionnaire considerations.
experiment_plan: Variant A (control): current symmetric per-token pricing with existing streaming behavior
Variant B: output-weighted pricing where output tokens billed at 1.25x input token rate; streaming connections that exceed 120s activate per-session minimum of 2,500 tokens billed
Variant C: output-weighted pricing at 1.5x with per-session minimum of 1,000 tokens and a 30s grace window to avoid penalizing short-lived connections
Rollout: start with 2% of eligible free-tier + self-serve customers for each variant, expand to 10% by week 3 if no major regressions
Eligibility: only non-enterprise accounts without committed pricing, exclude Dedicated/Private deployments
Telemetry: collect per-request direction (input/output), session duration, billed tokens, effective $/req, cancellation rates, support tickets labeled billing, and mean latency changes
Success analysis: compare median and 90th percentile effective bill across workloads, track % customers exposed to >20% bill change, and measure churn/upgrade signals over 30 days
success_criteria: Net revenue per active customer increases by >=4% without >5% of customers experiencing a >25% bill increase
No significant increase in billing-related support tickets (<=10% uplift vs baseline)
Positive NPS signal in a targeted post-experiment survey for sampled customers
Enterprise SQ reviewers confirm model is explainable and can be mapped to contract language
risks_mitigation: High-bill risk: apply a soft cap/alerts to prevent surprise invoices and provide an opt-out grace for the first invoice cycle
Billing complexity: add clear billing examples in Console and post-experiment UI copy; surface an estimator in the dashboard
Sales/Legal: coordinate with enterprise contracts team to draft FAQ language and add a one-line explanatory metric in SQ responses
Data skew: stratify analysis by workload archetype (chat, summarization, embeddings pipeline) to avoid misleading averages
